prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: low-speed head-on collision in Conroe, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported wrist fracture. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1347; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was traveling southbound on a two-lane roadway in Conroe, Texas, when the vehicle crossed into the northbound lane and made contact head-on with a sedan operated by Driver 2. The impact was low in speed, and both vehicles remained largely upright with no airbag deployment reported. Driver 1 stated that the left wrist struck the steering assembly during the collision, and the nature of the injury is consistent with that description and with the force of the contact observed at the scene. Driver 2 independently described the crash in the same sequence, and two independent witnesses gave statements that match. Officers photographed both vehicles, and the damage to the front end of each is consistent with a frontal impact of this type. No prior damage to either vehicle was noted in the reporting officer's review. The Passenger, seated in the front right seat, was present at the scene and confirmed to officers that Driver 1 was the operator at the time. Driver 1 is listed as a named insured on the policy covering the vehicle involved. No citations were issued at the scene pending further review.
